transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. [Your Name]. Well, I'm here because I just feel like I can't settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like... I always have this urge to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and really just need to be sitting still. It's exhausting.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually elevated, irritable, or feeling like you don’t need as much sleep lately?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood isn't elevated or unusually high. And I definitely need my sleep. Like I said, I'm completely worn out. It's just hard to actually sit still and get that rest, you know? But I certainly don't feel like I can just go without sleep, and I wouldn't say I'm irritable... mostly just tired of feeling this way.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I don't feel sad or anything like that. I still like my usual hobbies and such. It's just... well, like I said, the hard part is sitting still long enough to actually do them. But no, my mood is fine. I haven't been feeling down or losing interest.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious about a number of things, like work, health, or other everyday matters?

No, I don't really have that problem. I mean, I have normal everyday concerns, but I'm not excessively worried or anxious about my health or anything else. My mind isn't spinning with worries... it's really just that physical feeling of needing to be doing something, like I can't just sit and relax.
Do you ever feel a discomfort or restlessness in your legs when you try to sit still or lie down, like a crawling or tingling sensation that makes you want to move them?

No, I don't get anything like that. My legs don't tingle or crawl or feel uncomfortable like that. It's not a physical feeling in my legs specifically making me move them... it's just a general feeling of needing to be up and doing something. But no weird sensations in my legs.
Can you describe what it feels like when you can't sit still? Is it more of an inner restlessness or a mental push to keep moving, even when you know you should be resting?

It's definitely an inner restlessness. Honestly, that's really why I came in. I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like... well, I just have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still. It's just a constant push to keep going.
Is this inner restlessness something you feel all the time, even when you're not in situations where you need to be still, or does it mostly come up when you're trying to sit down or relax?

I'd say it's pretty much all the time. I mean... I guess I notice it the most when I actually try to sit down in my chair and relax, because that's when it really bothers me that I can't just be still. But even when I'm up and doing things around the house, I still feel that push. It's just always there, like my motor is always running, no matter what I'm doing.
Have you ever experienced periods where your restlessness was so intense that it significantly interfered with your ability to function at work, socially, or in other important areas of your life?

Yes, it definitely interferes with things. It's gotten to the point where my family has actually had to step in and take over dealing with my bills and paperwork because I just can't sit down and focus on them. And socially... well, it's affected my volunteer work. The people at my church and the community garden have had to redo plans or cover for responsibilities I ended up dropping. I just couldn't stay on track with what I promised to do. It makes me feel really embarrassed, honestly, because these are groups I care about, and now they feel like they can't count on me anymore.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I always have that restless feeling, like I said, but it's not like I feel unusually energetic. It's actually pretty exhausting. And I definitely don't feel like I need less sleep. I'd love to get good rest, I just have a hard time settling down to get it. But no, I haven't had any periods like what you're describing where I just didn't need to sleep at all.
Does the inner restlessness cause you distress or impair your ability to function in any other areas of your life besides handling bills, paperwork, and your volunteer work?

No, I don't think so. I mean, the bills and the volunteering are the main things it really messes up. It's definitely distressing just... having to live with that constant restless feeling every single day, but as far as other specific areas where I can't function, I can't really think of anything else right now. Just what I already told you.
Has anyone else, like family members or friends, commented on your restlessness or the way you're constantly moving, even when you're not aware of it yourself?

Yes, they definitely have. It's... well, it happens a lot, actually. Even in church meetings, I'll be tapping my foot, or just rubbing the edge of my purse over and over. Or I'm constantly shifting around in my chair. I don't always realize I'm doing it, but then the ladies sitting beside me will start looking over at me. They don't always say something right away, but I can tell it's distracting them, and they've definitely pointed it out to me after.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or experienced any issues with your sleep, such as insomnia or sleep apnea?

No, I've never been diagnosed with any of that. No sleep apnea or anything. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I do have a hard time settling down at night because I just feel so restless, but I've never had a doctor tell me I have insomnia or a specific sleep disorder. It's really just that trouble winding down.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually good, like you were on top of the world, or where you were much more talkative, active, or confident than usual?

No, I haven't ever experienced anything like that. I mean, I have regular good days, of course, but nothing where I feel... unusually high or on top of the world for days on end. And I don't suddenly get super confident or way more talkative than usual. It's really just my normal everyday self.

Have you ever had a period where your restlessness was accompanied by a noticeably elevated or irritable mood, along with other changes like much more talking than usual, racing thoughts, or doing things that were out of character for you, even for a few days?

No, I can't say that I have. My restlessness is just... it's just always there, you know? It doesn't really come with any sudden mood changes or feeling irritable or anything like that. And I don't have racing thoughts or start doing things that are completely out of character. It's just that constant need to move, not a whole shift in how I'm acting or feeling.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so good or so energized that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even if it didn't last very long?

No, really, I haven't. I don't get these bursts of energy where I feel different from my usual self. Like I said, the restlessness is just kind of my normal. I don't have periods where I feel incredibly energized or unusually good, not even for a short time. It's just... I'm just me, just with that hard time sitting still.
Do you ever notice that the restless feeling in your body gets worse in the evening or at night, or when you're sitting for a long time, like on a car ride or at a desk?

No, I haven't really noticed it being worse in the evening or at night. It's pretty much just there all the time. I mean, sitting for a long time is always hard for me, whether it's morning or night, but the restless feeling itself doesn't really change or flare up at a certain time of day. It's just a constant thing I deal with.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so unusually good or energized that other people noticed a change in your behavior or felt you were not your usual self, even if it only lasted a few hours?

No, doctor, I really haven't. Like I was saying, I don't get those kinds of highs. Nobody has ever told me I was acting unusually energized or out of character, not even for a few hours. It's just my normal, everyday self... just with that constant fidgeting and trouble keeping still. I don't have these spikes where I suddenly act like a different person.
Do you feel restless specifically when you're trying to fall asleep, or does it ease up at all once you're actually in bed and ready to sleep?

Well, I wouldn't say it happens specifically when I'm trying to fall asleep. It doesn't really ease up much either, to be honest. It's just... kind of the same. I mean, I might toss and turn a bit just because I'm always a fidgety person, but getting into bed doesn't make it worse or trigger anything new. It's just my usual restlessness, same as during the day.
